question: Should OpenClaw bundle an agent-facing broker that deliberately exposes approved raw secret values to the active model, with transcript-only redaction and optional long-lived standing grants?
rationale: Tests can verify mechanics, but they cannot decide whether raw model visibility and the default durable-authorization policy are acceptable core security boundaries.

options.title: Harden and sponsor
options.body: Approve the bundled security model after field-scoped retrieval, command-only setup repair, grant-policy review, and redacted live proof are complete.

options.title: Narrow the capability
options.body: Limit the plugin to executing approved credential-bound actions so raw secret values never enter general model context.

options.title: Keep it external
options.body: Leave agent-facing 1Password access as an external plugin until the security boundary has broader operational evidence.

recommendation.title: Harden and sponsor
recommendation.body: Approve the bundled security model after field-scoped retrieval, command-only setup repair, grant-policy review, and redacted live proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and secops signal make steipete the strongest owner for the plugin/security boundary decision.
